question: Does a static board-price profile change promotion-target ordering in a real StagedMovePicker caller on retained legal trajectories, enough to justify one fresh utility panel?
scope: Mechanism reachability only: reconstruct the already-frozen 64 5x5 game records across the eight recorded generated RuleSets; no new games, no utility inference, no default change.
method: At each replayed pre-action state enumerate legal promotion actions and compare actual StagedMovePicker output for the same Unit profile with the isolated static-board-only type_value profile. Assert full action/replay legality and that capture_order_value and leaf evaluate are identical between adapters; report affected states, distinct target rankings, rule/owner/parity coverage and counts.
decision: If the actual optional caller has no reachable promotion-target ordering differences or coverage is confined to one stratum, close this branch. If multiple rules and both owners/parities show changes, consider one fresh preregistered utility panel only if promotion-ordering utility could change whether the staged picker remains an optional candidate; this preflight itself cannot establish utility.
completion: All records reconstructed or an explicit failure retained; report exact counts and limitations.
